extracted.intended_audience: users of the PARI/GP library (computational number theorists, mathematicians, and programmers using PARI/GP)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP number-field and relative-number-field routines: function signatures, required input shapes, flags, returned results and notable warnings (precision, performance, special cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfgaloisapply(nf, aut, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given nf from nfinit and aut a Galois automorphism (expressed as a polynomial or a polmod), computes the action of aut on x in the number field. x can be an element (scalar, polmod, polynomial, column vector), an ideal (by ZK-generators or Z-basis), a prime ideal (5-element row), or an idele (2-element row). Other vector or matrix arguments are forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use galoisapply(nf, aut, x). Note: aut must be an automorphism found e.g. via nfgaloisconj variants. Because elements and ideals can be confused, avoid passing arbitrary vectors/matrices. The automorphism can be provided as polynomial/polmod; variable conventions of nf and polmods must match other nf routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfgaloisconj(nf, {flag = 0}, {d})
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes conjugates of a root r of the polynomial nf[1] expressed as polynomials in r. Works even if nf is not Galois (some conjugates may lie in the field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: galoisconj0(nf, flag, d, prec); convenience wrappers galoisconj(nf), galoisconj2(nf,n,prec), galoisconj4(nf,d). Flag meanings: flag=0 default (uses combination of flags 4 and 1 for number fields; else 4 and 2 but may be incomplete), flag=1 uses nfroots (requires number field), flag=2 uses complex approximations + integral LLL (may miss conjugates; increase precision if missing), flag=4 uses Allombert's algorithm + permutation testing and returns full automorphism list for fields with "weakly" super solvable Galois group, else just identity. d (if present) is assumed multiple of denominators of conjugate polynomials. Note: flag=4 is effective for quickly checking Galois-ness for polynomials of degree <36 and faster than nfroots for high degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfhilbert(nf, a, b, {pr})
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute global Hilbert symbol (a,b) in nf (value 1 if x^2 - a y^2 - b z^2 has a nontrivial solution in nf, -1 otherwise). If pr provided, compute local symbol modulo prime ideal pr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: nf_hilbert(nf, a, b, pr) where omitted pr is coded as NULL. pr should be in format as output by idealprimedec.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfhnf(nf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a pseudo-matrix (A,I), finds a pseudo-basis in Hermite normal form of the module it generates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: nf_hermite(nf, x). Returns HNF pseudo-basis for the module generated by (A,I).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfhnfmod(nf, x, detx)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a pseudo-matrix (A,I) and an ideal detx contained in (an integral multiple of) the determinant, finds a pseudo-basis in Hermite normal form of the generated module while avoiding coefficient explosion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: nf_heritemod(nf, x, detx). detx can be computed by nfdetint.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfinit(pol, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Initializes a number field structure nf from pol ∈ Z[X] (preferably monic irreducible). nf is a technical 9-component row vector containing polynomial, signature, discriminant, index, various matrices (M, MC, T2, T, MD, TI, MDI), roots, integral basis, power-basis matrix, multiplication table, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer accessing nf components via member names (nf.pol, nf.sign, nf.disc, nf.index, nf.t2, nf.roots, nf.zk, etc.) since internal organization may change. If non-monic input, nfinit will transform to monic and possibly polred (see flags). Special input [x,B] allowed (polynomial plus integer basis). Flag bits: flag=2 applies polred to change to simpler polynomial and uses it for subsequent computations; flag=3 does polred and outputs [nf, Mod(a,P)] (change of variables), flags 4/5 are partial polred variants. Library syntax: nf_init0(x, flag, prec). Note: accepted inputs include nf or bnf (not generally useful). Performance note: round 4 algorithm default may be slow in pathological cases; consider nfbasis(x,2) round 2 in such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfisideal(nf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns 1 if x is an ideal in the number field nf, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: isideal(x). Use to test ideal-ness of arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfisincl(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests whether number field K defined by polynomial x is conjugate to a subfield of field L defined by y. Outputs 0 if not; otherwise returns vector of polynomials a giving embeddings (y | x ◦ a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If y is a number field (nf), a much faster algorithm is used (factor x over y using nffactor). Historically required flag; now returns all embeddings. Library syntax: nf_isincl(x, y, flag). Inputs must be in Q[X] unless using nf form.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfisisom(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests whether two number fields defined by x and y are isomorphic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If either x or y is a number field, a faster algorithm is used. Library syntax: nf_isisom(x, y, flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfnewprec(nf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms the number field nf into corresponding data at current (usually larger) precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works as expected if nf is actually a bnf (updates bnf to current precision) but may be slow due to needing many principal ideal generator computations. Library syntax: nf_newprec(nf, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfkermodpr(nf, a, pr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes kernel of matrix a in ZK/pr where pr is in modpr format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: nf_kermodpr(nf, a, pr). See nfmodprinit for modpr format.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfmodprinit(nf, pr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms prime ideal pr into modpr format necessary for modulo-pr operations in nf. Returns [P, a], where P is HNF of pr and a is integral element congruent to 1 mod pr and 0 mod p/pre (p=Z∩pr, e absolute ramification index).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: nf_modprinit(nf, pr). Use before any computations modulo pr to prepare modpr structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfsubfields(nf, {d = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Finds all subfields of degree d of number field nf (all subfields if d omitted or 0). Result: vector of subfields each [g,h] where g absolute equation and h expresses roots relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crude implementation by M. Olivier of Klüners' algorithm. Library syntax: subfields(nf, d).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfroots(nf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes roots of polynomial x in number field nf (from nfinit), without multiplicity. x coefficients can be in the number field (scalar, polmod, polynomial, column vector).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main variable of nf must be lower priority (greater variable number) than that of x. If number-field coefficients occur explicitly as polmods within x, the variable of those polmods must be same as main variable of t (see nffactor). Library syntax: nf_roots(nf, x).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfrootsof1(nf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes number of roots of unity w and a primitive w-th root of unity (expressed on integral basis) belonging to nf. Returns [w, z] where z is column vector on nf.zk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rootsof1(nf).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfsnf(nf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a torsion module x as 3-component [A,I,J] (A invertible n×n matrix, I and J ideal lists), outputs Smith normal form ideal list d1,...,dn such that x ≅ ZK/d1 ⊕ ... ⊕ ZK/dn with di dividing di-1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: If ei canonical basis, I=[b1..bn], J=[a1..an], then x ≅ (⊕ bi ei)/(⊕ ai Aj) where Aj are columns of A. Every finitely generated torsion module can be given in this way. Library syntax: nf_smith(nf, x).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfsolvemodpr(nf, a, b, pr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solves a · x = b in ZK/pr where a is matrix and b column vector; pr is in modpr format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: nf_solvemodpr(nf, a, b, pr). Prepare pr via nfmodprinit.

rubrics_metrics.name: polcompositum(x, y, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given polynomials x and y in Z[X] in same variable, outputs vector listing all possible composita of number fields defined by x and y (or étale algebras if squarefree). Errors if either polynomial not squarefree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one polynomial irreducible (say x), often faster to compute nffactor(nfinit(x), y) then rnfequation. If flag=1 outputs vector of 4-component [z,a,b,k] with z compositum polynomial, a and b express roots, and k small integer s.t. a+kb chosen root. Compositum polynomials can be complicated; advisable to polred (reduce) before further computations. Library syntax: polcompositum0(x,y,flag). Example in docs demonstrates reduction via polredabs and substitution to obtain simpler representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: polgalois(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes Galois group of non-constant polynomial x ∈ Q[X]. In version described, x must be irreducible and deg(x) ≤ 7 (larger degrees supported with additional resolvent data). Output is [n, s, k] with n=group size, s=signature (1 if subgroup of An else -1), k=index among groups with same (n,s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method: resolvent polynomials; sensitive to precision — precision updated internally but rare wrong results possible if initial precision insufficient. Library syntax: galois(x, prec). Groups enumerated for degrees 1..7 with standard group names and their [n,s,k] codes (document gives explicit mapping).

rubrics_metrics.name: polred(x, {flag = 0}, {p})
rubrics_metrics.description: Finds polynomials with reasonably small coefficients defining subfields of number field defined by x. One polynomial always defines Q, another defines same field as x if irreducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts same inputs as nfinit (non-monic polynomials, nf, bnf, [x,ZK basis]). Flag binary digits: 1 = partial reduction only (may use suborder), 2 = also returns elements (two-column matrix: elements and minimal polynomials). If p provided, assumed two-column factorization matrix of discriminant of x. Library syntax: polred0(x, flag, p, prec); convenience polred(x, prec) and factoredpolred(x,p,prec) (flag=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: polredabs(x, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Finds a polynomial defining same number field as x with minimal T2-norm (sum squares of moduli of roots). Accepts same inputs as nfinit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag bits: 1 = output [P,a] where P is default and a is element expressed on root of P whose minimal polynomial is x; 4 = give all polynomials of minimal T2 norm (between P(x) and P(-x) only one given by default). Library syntax: polredabs0(x, flag, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: polredord(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Finds polynomials with reasonably small coefficients and same degree as x defining suborders of order defined by x. One polynomial always defines Q and another defines same order as x if irreducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: ordred(x). Useful for finding simpler defining polynomials of the same order (not necessarily maximal).

rubrics_metrics.name: poltschirnhaus(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies a random Tschirnhausen transformation to separable non-constant polynomial x to obtain a new equation for the étale algebra defined by x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when computing resolvents; used by polgalois. Library syntax: tschirnhaus(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfalgtobasis(rnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given relative number field extension rnf (output of rnfinit) and x an element of L expressed as polynomial or polmod with polmod coefficients, expresses x on the relative integral basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_algtobasis(rnf, x). Use to convert polmod representations to basis coordinates in relative extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfbasis(bnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a big number field bnf (from bnfinit) and either polynomial x with coefficients in bnf defining a relative extension L or a pseudo-basis x of such an extension, returns either a true bnf-basis of L if exists, or an n+1-element generating set of L otherwise (n = rank of L over bnf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_basis(bnf, x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfbasistoalg(rnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given relative extension rnf and x expressed on the relative integral basis, computes representation of x as polmod with polmod coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_basistoalg(rnf, x). Use when a polmod representation is needed from basis coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfcharpoly(nf, T, a, {v = x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristic polynomial of a over nf where a belongs to algebra defined by T over nf (i.e., nf[X]/(T)). Returns polynomial in variable v (x by default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_charpoly(nf, T, a, v) where v is a variable number. Ensure variable priority conventions between nf and T as usual.

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfconductor(bnf, pol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a big number field bnf and a relative polynomial pol defining an Abelian extension, computes class field theory conductor of this Abelian extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns [conductor, rayclgp, subgroup] where conductor is [f0,f∞], rayclgp is ray class group [h,cyc,gen], and subgroup is matrix in HNF defining subgroup of ray class group on given generators. Library syntax: rnf_conductor(rnf, pol, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfdedekind(nf, pol, pr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates relative Dedekind criterion over the order defined by a root of pol for prime ideal pr and outputs 3-component vector: flag (1 if enlarged order is pr-maximal, 0 otherwise), pseudo-basis of enlarged order, valuation at pr of order discriminant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_dedekind(nf, pol, pr). nf must be from nfinit and pr a prime ideal of nf; pol has coefficients in nf defining relative extension L.

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfdet(nf, M)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a pseudomatrix M over maximal order of nf, computes its pseudo-determinant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_det(nf, M).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfdisc(nf, pol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given nf (from nfinit) and polynomial pol with coefficients in nf defining relative extension L, computes relative discriminant of L: two-element row [D,d] where D is relative ideal discriminant and d is relative discriminant as element of nf^*/nf^{*2}. Main variable of nf must be lower priority than that of pol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: nf may be a bnf as usual. Library syntax: rnf_discf(bnf, pol).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfeltabstorel(rnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given relative extension rnf and x an element of L expressed as polynomial modulo the absolute equation rnf[11][1], computes x as element of the relative extension L/K as polmod with polmod coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_elementabstorel(rnf, x). Useful for converting absolute-polynomial representations to relative-polmod representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfeltdown(rnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given rnf and x element of L expressed as polynomial or polmod with polmod coefficients, computes x as an element of K as a polmod, assuming x is in K (error otherwise). If x given on relative integral basis, apply rnfbasistoalg first, else PARI will treat as vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_elementdown(rnf, x). Use rnfbasistoalg if input is basis coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfeltreltoabs(rnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given rnf and x element of L expressed as polynomial/polmod with polmod coefficients, computes x as element of absolute extension L/Q as polynomial modulo absolute equation rnf[11][1]. If x on relative integral basis, apply rnfbasistoalg first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_elementreltoabs(rnf, x). Be careful with representation types to avoid PARI misinterpreting vectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfeltup(rnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given rnf and x an element of K expressed as polynomial or polmod, computes x as an element of absolute extension L/Q as polynomial modulo absolute equation rnf[11][1]. If x given on integral basis of K, apply nfbasistoalg first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_elementup(rnf, x). Note: if x is already in relative extension L/K its expression is identical; unnecessary conversions can be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfequation(nf, pol, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given nf (from nfinit or a polynomial) and polynomial pol with coefficients in nf defining relative extension L, computes the absolute equation of L over Q. If flag non-zero, outputs [z, a, k] where z absolute equation, a polmod expressing root β of pol in terms of θ (root of z), and k small integer with θ = β + k α where α is generator of base field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main variable of nf must be lower priority than that of pol. For efficiency, function checks squarefreeness not irreducibility; if reducible but squarefree, result is absolute equation of étale algebra. If pol not squarefree, error issued. Library syntax: rnf_equation0(nf, pol, flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfhnfbasis(bnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given big number field bnf and either polynomial x with coefficients in bnf defining relative extension L or pseudo-basis x, returns true bnf-basis of L in upper triangular Hermite normal form if it exists, zero otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_hermitebasis(nf, x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealabstorel(rnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given rnf and x an ideal of absolute extension L/Q given in HNF, computes relative pseudomatrix in HNF giving ideal x considered as ideal of relative extension L/K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x not in HNF, apply idealhnf first. Library syntax: rnf_idealabstorel(rnf, x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealdown(rnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given rnf and x an ideal of absolute extension L/Q given in HNF, returns the ideal of K below x (intersection x ∩ K). If x already given as relative ideal (pseudomatrix in HNF), result is simply first ideal of ideal list of pseudomatrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_idealdown(rnf, x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealhnf(rnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given rnf and x a relative ideal (many possible input types), computes relative Hermite normal form as 2-component row vector: [HNF matrix (entries on integral basis), ideals].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_idealhermite(rnf, x). Ensure input ideal type is accepted (elements, pseudomatrices, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealmul(rnf, x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given rnf and x,y ideals of relative extension L/K given by pseudo-matrices, outputs the ideal product as a relative ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_idealmul(rnf, x, y).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealnormabs(rnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given rnf and x a relative ideal (various types), computes the norm of x considered as ideal of absolute extension L/Q (faster variant of idealnorm(rnfidealnormrel(rnf,x))).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_idealnormabs(rnf, x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealnormrel(rnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given rnf and x a relative ideal, computes the relative norm of x as ideal of K in HNF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_idealnormrel(rnf, x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealreltoabs(rnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given rnf and x a relative ideal, computes HNF matrix of ideal x considered as ideal of absolute extension L/Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_idealreltoabs(rnf, x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealtwoelt(rnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given rnf and x an ideal of relative extension given by a pseudo-matrix, returns vector of two generators of x over ZL expressed as polmods with polmod coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_idealtwoelement(rnf, x). Useful to produce explicit two-element generators for ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealup(rnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given rnf and x an ideal of K, gives the ideal xZL as an absolute ideal of L/Q; relative ideal representation trivial (matrix identity and ideal list starts with x and others ZK).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_idealup(rnf, x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfinit(nf, pol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given base field nf (nfinit format) and pol polynomial defining relative extension over nf, computes all data needed to work in the relative extension. Main variable of pol must be higher priority (lower number) than that of nf and coefficients of pol must be in nf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result is 11-component row vector describing relative equation, local embedding data, relative discriminant, index, relative integral pseudo-basis, inverse integral basis matrix, absolute equation and absolute basis info, among others. See doc for detailed structure: rnf[1] relative polynomial, rnf[2] embedding multiplicities vector, rnf[3] [d(L/K), s], rnf[4] index f, rnf[5] vm vector of matrices for embeddings and T2 matrices, rnf[6] roots per embedding, rnf[7] relative integral pseudobasis and HNF ideal list, rnf[8] inverse integral-basis matrix, rnf[9] (may be multiplication table), rnf[10]=nf, rnf[11] vabs absolute data ([abs equation, expr of generator, k shift, absolute integral basis, inverse matrix]). Library syntax: rnf_initalg(nf, pol, prec). Warning: be careful if k ≠ 0 when mixing absolute and relative quantities; consider changing relative polynomial so its root is β + k α (example substitution provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfisfree(bnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given big number field bnf (bnfinit) and polynomial x or pseudo-basis defining relative extension L/bnf, returns 1 if L/bnf is free, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_isfree(bnf, x). Output is a long (integer).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfisnorm(bnf, ext, el, {flag = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative analogue of bnfisnorm: tries to decide whether element el in bnf is norm of some y in ext. ext is a relative extension row vector with ext[1] relative equation, ext[2] generator expression, ext[3] bnfinit of absolute extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns vector [a, b] where el = Norm(a) * b. Searches for S-integer solution with S containing ramified primes, generators of class group of ext, and primes dividing el. If ext/bnf known Galois, set flag=0 (el is norm iff b=1). If flag ≠ 0, add to S primes dividing flag (if flag<0) or primes less than flag (if flag>0). Guarantee of correctness (el is norm iff b=1) holds under GRH if S contains all primes < 12 log2 |disc(Ext)| where Ext is normal closure of ext/bnf. Library syntax: rnf_isnorm(bnf, ext, x, flag, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfkummer(bnr, subgroup, {deg = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given bnr as output of bnrinit, finds a relative equation for class field corresponding to the module in bnr and given congruence subgroup. If deg>0, outputs list of all relative equations of degree deg contained in ray class field defined by bnr. (Program in development).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_kummer(bnr, subgroup, deg, prec) where deg is long. Note: still under development; use with caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: rnflllgram(nf, pol, order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given polynomial pol with coefficients in nf and an order 'order' (output by rnfpseudobasis or similar), returns [[neworder], U] where neworder is reduced order and U is unimodular transformation matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: rnf_lllgram(nf, pol, order, prec). Uses LLL-like reduction for orders over number fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfnormgroup(bnr, pol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given bnr (big ray class field from bnrinit) and pol a relative polynomial defining an Abelian extension, computes the norm group (Artin/Takagi group) corresponding to the Abelian extension of bnf = bnr[1] defined by pol. Assumes module of bnr is a multiple of conductor; does not verify Abelian assumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result is HNF defining norm group on given generators of bnr[5][3]. If assumptions incorrect, result undefined. Library syntax: rnf_normgroup(bnr, pol).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfpolred(nf, pol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative version of polred: given monic polynomial pol with coefficients in nf, finds list of relative polynomials defining some subfields, hopefully simpler and containing original field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In described version (2.0.19), slower than rnfpolredabs. Library syntax: rnf_polred(nf, pol, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfpolredabs(nf, pol, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative version of polredabs: given monic pol with coefficients in nf, finds a simpler relative polynomial defining same field. If flag=1 returns [P,a] where a is element on root of P whose characteristic polynomial is pol; if flag=2 returns an absolute polynomial (same as rnfequation(rnfpolredabs(...)) but faster).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation is both faster and more efficient than rnfpolred in practice because rnfpolred relies on incomplete lattice reduction theory (rnflllgram). Library syntax: rnf_polredabs(nf, pol, flag, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfpseudobasis(nf, pol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given nf and polynomial pol with coefficients in nf defining relative extension L, computes a pseudo-basis (A,I) and relative discriminant of L; output [A, I, D, d] where D relative ideal discriminant, d discriminant as element of nf^*/nf^{*2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: nf can be a bnf as usual. Library syntax: rnf_pseudobasis(nf, pol).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfsteinitz(nf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given nf and polynomial x (or pseudo-basis x) defining relative extension L, computes another pseudo-basis (A,I) (not necessarily HNF) such that all ideals in I except perhaps last are equal to ring of integers of nf; outputs [A, I, D, d] as in rnfpseudobasis. The Steinitz class is class of last ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: nf can be a bnf. Library syntax: rnf_steinitz(nf, x). Useful to determine Steinitz class of extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: subgrouplist(bnr, {bound}, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given bnr (output by bnrinit) or list of cyclic components of finite Abelian group G, outputs list of subgroups of G (optionally bounded by index bound). Subgroups are given as HNF left divisors of SNF matrix for G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=0 (default) and bnr from bnrinit, returns only subgroups whose modulus is the conductor. Library syntax: subgrouplist0(bnr, bound, flag, prec) with bound, flag, prec longs.

rubrics_metrics.name: zetak(znf, x, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given znf (number field initialized by zetakinit), computes value of Dedekind zeta function of number field at complex number x. If flag=1 computes Dedekind Λ function instead (zeta multiplied by gamma and exponential factors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy depends on accuracy of zetakinit and current precision; results may be off by up to 5-10 decimal digits. Library syntax: glambdak(znf, x, prec) or gzetak(znf, x, prec). Use caution with required precision and zetakinit initialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: zetakinit(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes initialization data for number field defined by polynomial x so as to compute Dedekind zeta and lambda functions (calls bnfinit). Result is 9-component vector v whose components are technical and intended to be used only through zetak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only component sometimes useful directly is v[1][4] from bnfinit. Function is very inefficient and should be rewritten; it needs to compute millions of Dirichlet series coefficients at high precision. For fields with large discriminant it cannot handle more than about 9 digits of relative precision at default resources (e.g., zetakinit(x^8-2) needs ~440MB memory at default precision). Library syntax: initzeta(x).
